errors.claim: India safeguards almost all its young children before their second birthday.
errors.reason: The indicator measures vaccination before 12 months or at any time before the survey, not specifically before the second birthday.

errors.claim: leaving most young children without a dose.
errors.reason: With 23% coverage, 77% are unvaccinated, which is most, but the claim implies this is a direct consequence of being the lowest, whereas the indicator definition does not provide causal history.

claims.text: India protects 97% of children against measles.
Germany has 96%, Japan 95%, Brazil 93%, and USA 92%.

title.reason: The title frames a comparison between two countries with vastly different coverage rates.

hook.reason: The hook introduces the topic of measles protection.

description.reason: The description accurately reflects the high global coverage and Montenegro's outlier status.

beat_1.reason: The indicator definition does not specify the second birthday as the cutoff.

beat_2.reason: Calculation is mathematically accurate based on the evidence.

beat_3.reason: While the rank is correct, the causal claim about the consequence is not supported by the definition.

beat_4.reason: Median and individual country values are correct.

card_5.reason: The card displays the indicator and source.
